hypothesis: If the claim holds, most women stop menstruating at about forty, with a tail that reaches about fifty, and childbearing is recorded through the forties.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. This test cannot return supports. The NCHS birth-rate table's oldest age group is 45-49 years, so it has no bin for births beyond fifty, and a universal negative ('no case on record' past that age) is unscored. A menopause pattern that matches the claim is therefore mixed, not a pass. Match would have required, and is reported but not allowed to pass: weighted median of RHQ060 in [38, 43] and weighted 90th percentile in [48, 55], among women with RHD043 = 7 (Menopause/Change of life) and RHQ060 in 20-59, age at interview >= 20, WTINT2YR > 0, n >= 100. The weighted percentile is the smallest age at which cumulative interview weight reaches the stated fraction of total weight.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refuted if the weighted median age at last menstrual period, in the set above, is >= 47 or <= 35, with n >= 100. Those medians are not 'about forty' for most women. Mixed if the median is in (35, 47) and the fail rule does not apply, including a median inside [38, 43], because the beyond-fifty clause is unmeasured. Inconclusive with reason underpowered if n < 100, and data-unavailable if RHQ060, RHD043 or the weights cannot be retrieved. Birth rates at 40-44 and 45-49 in the latest year of the NCHS table are reported and do not set the verdict. Codes 19 and 60 on RHQ060 are censored labels and are excluded.

test_contract.expected_observation: Among women who report natural menopause, the center of the age-at-last-period distribution is about 40 and the upper tail reaches about 50.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The weighted median age at natural menopause is 47 or older, or 35 or younger.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A public survey that separates natural menopause from hysterectomy and records age at last period in years, plus a public vital-statistics series of birth rates by maternal age. NHANES 2017-2018 and the NCHS birth-rate table are the named files. The birth-rate table is admissible only as a description of ages it actually bins.
test_contract.inference_method: Weighted median and weighted 90th percentile on WTINT2YR, restricted to RHD043 code 7. The verdict compares the median with fixed ages taken from the sentence (about forty, versus a center nearer fifty). Birth rates are not a test of the universal negative past fifty.

interpretation: 'About their fortieth year' is the center of the distribution, operationalized as a weighted median from 38 through 43. A median of 47 or more means most women have not stopped near forty. 'Even to the fiftieth year' is the upper tail. 'No case beyond that age' would require birth counts at 51 or older; the birth-rate file stops at 45-49, which was established from the age-group labels before any rate was used, so that clause is not scored. RHD190 is top-coded at 45 in the NHANES codebook and is not used.
caveats: Codebook value labels for RHD043, RHQ060 and RHD190 were read before registration, including the fact that RHD190 collapses 45 and older into one code and that RHQ060's numeric values are labelled as a 20-to-59 range. The median was not computed and the XPT was not downloaded. Age-group labels of the NCHS birth-rate table were listed before registration; rates were not used to set thresholds.
